hook: A runner covers more ground in some minutes than in others. Comparing how fast two quantities change together, over a few minutes, is the first step to describing any function.

prereq.q: What is the slope of the line through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$?
In polar coordinates, what is $x$ for the point $(r, \theta) = (2, 0)$?

chain.cause: Divide the change in output by the change in input
chain.effect: the average rate of change on $[a, b]$

chain.cause: Shrink the interval around a point
chain.effect: the average rates estimate how fast $f$ changes there

ideas: The average rate of change is the slope of the secant line.
A positive rate means the output rises as the input rises.

misconception.wrong: The average rate of change is the average of the two outputs.
misconception.right: It is the change in output divided by the change in input.

summary: The average rate of change of $f$ on $[a, b]$ is $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$, the slope of the secant line. Over small nearby intervals it compares how fast a function changes at two points.
